description:
Army Contracting Command-Aberdeen Proving Ground (ACC-APG), in support of the Capability Program Executive (CPE) Enterprise Software and Service (ES2) (formerly known as Program Executive Office (PEO) Enterprise), intends to award a Multiple Award (MA) Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract, MAPS. This is the follow-on and combination of the ACC-APG Responsive Strategic Sourcing for Services (RS3) and Product Lead (PL) Digital Market’s Information Technology Enterprise Solutions – 3 Services (ITES-3S) IDIQ Contract Vehicles. The objective of the MAPS IDIQ contract is to provide Army customers, Portfolio Acquisition Executives (PAE), CPEs, Department of War (DoW) agencies, and other federal agencies with uncommon knowledge-based professional services and support the Army enterprise infrastructure and infostructure goals with information technology (IT) services worldwide (inside the contiguous United States (CONUS) and outside the contiguous United States (OCONUS)), including hostile areas. By combining these vehicles, the Army aims to enhance flexibility, reduce redundancy, and improve cost-efficiency in acquiring uncommon knowledge-based professional services. This integration will also ensure a unified approach in meeting the Army’s evolving technology and strategic needs, thus optimizing mission readiness and effectiveness. 

 Please note, due to system constraints within sam.gov it only allowed one NAICS to be identified; however, this acquisition contains five primary NAICS codes as identified in the solicitation.  

  

   AMENDMENT 0012 UPDATE:   This notice announces the issuance of Amendment 0012 to the MAPS Solicitation (Solicitation W15P7T26RA006). The purpose of the Amendment is to allow for Small Businesses and Commercial-Sector Vendor Small Businesses to submit offers in the construct of a Small Business Teaming Arrangement (SBTA). Only SBTA Offerors are permitted to submit proposals in response to MAPS Solicitation Amendment 0012. No other business type (to include Small Businesses or Commercial-Sector Vendors who are proposing outside of an SBTA) are permitted to propose or modify their prior submissions. A Small Business or Commercial-Sector Vendor Offeror that previously submitted a proposal under this Solicitation as a Prime Offeror may withdraw their existing proposal and submit a new proposal as an SBTA. Please refer to the attached Solicitation for all instructions, terms, and conditions.  

  PLEASE NOTE:  

  - ALL SBTA proposals MUST be resubmitted utilizing latest version of Solicitation and Attachments.   

  - On the SF33 block 3, W15P7T26RA0060012 is identified. The Solicitation Number is W15P7T26RA006 and has not changed. The "0012" at the end is the Amendment Number.   

 **Only SBTA Offerors are permitted to submit proposals in response to MAPS Solicitation Amendment 0012. No separate acknowledgment is required for non-SBTA Offerors.** 

  

  THE BELOW INFORMATION IS RETAINED FOR HISTORICAL PURPOSES:  

  UPDATE:  

 The Government is extending the proposal due date to  Monday November 30th at 11:59:59 AM  in preparation for the release of Amendment 0012. We encourage offerors to  not  submit proposals until they review Amendment 0012. 

  

   CLARIFICATION NOTE TO ATTACHMENT 0007 — 21 OCTOBER 2026   

  Section L.1 of the Solicitation (page 200), incorrectly references the Notice of Withdrawal Form as Attachment 0006 in two instances. The correct attachment number is  Attachment 0007 .  

  

   CLARIFICATION NOTE TO ATTACHMENT 0007 — 16 OCTOBER 2026   

  Offerors that previously submitted timely proposals may withdraw their proposal(s) utilizing Attachment 0007. Offerors shall use this Attachment to communicate to the Government which domain(s) from its prior proposal it now desires to withdraw from.  If an offeror submitted proposals for multiple domains, withdrawal from one (1) domain does not withdraw its proposals from the other domains. Only the domains identified on the form will be withdrawn. Withdrawal from a domain, will remove that specific domain's proposal in its entirety.  

   Example:  Company A submitted timely proposals for all five domains. Company A now intends to submit a proposal as an SBTA offeror for the Emerging IT domain. Company A must complete and submit Attachment 0007 identifying the Emerging IT domain for withdrawal. Company A must then submit a new SBTA proposal for the Emerging IT domain.   Company A’s previously submitted proposals for the other four domains remain valid, and no action is required for those domains.  

  This clarification does not amend the solicitation or its attachments.
